back: Timber from deciduous, broad-leaved trees. Slow-growing, so generally more expensive.
Timber from coniferous trees with needles and cones, usually evergreen. Fast-growing, so cheaper and more readily available.

front: Do 'hardwood' and 'softwood' describe how hard the timber is?
back: No — they describe the type of tree. Balsa is a hardwood but extremely soft.

front: How to tell hardwoods and softwoods apart
back: Look at the tree's leaves or needles. On a cut piece, softwoods are usually pale and resinous with knots; hardwoods often have finer grain. Weight and hardness are not reliable tests.
A man-made sheet made from layers, particles or fibres of wood bonded with adhesive under heat and pressure.
Natural timber has attractive grain but can warp, split and has knots; boards come in large, stable, uniform sheets, are cheaper and use waste wood.
Drying timber in the air or a kiln to reduce moisture, so it does not shrink, warp or split later.
Hardwood; pale pinkish-brown, close grain. Hard, very tough, good for turning and steam bending — toys, chairs, kitchen utensils.
Hardwood; very pale, extremely light and soft, cut with a craft knife — model making and prototypes.
Softwood; pale yellow with reddish rings, often knotty. Strong, light, cheap — construction, joists, budget furniture.
Softwood; pale with red or brown streaks and few knots. Hard and strong for a softwood but can warp — staircases and interior joinery.
Thin veneers glued with the grain of each layer at 90° to the next, always an odd number of layers.
Strong in all directions, stable, available in exterior and marine grades — but edges show the layers, thin face veneer, can splinter.
Fine wood fibres mixed with resin adhesive and pressed into sheets under heat and pressure.
Smooth both sides, no grain, cheap, stable, laser cuts cleanly — but absorbs water and swells, heavy, poor screw holding in edges, harmful dust.

front: In which direction is timber strongest?

back: How readily a material soaks up moisture. MDF is very absorbent; marine plywood resists water.
How easily a material can be cut, shaped, joined and finished using tools and machines.
